The guardian of the minor petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.7,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the minor petitioner in the road traffic accident that took place on 03.12.2018.
2. The brief facts of the case of the minor petitioner as follows:

On 03.12.2018 at about4.30 p.m., while minor petitioner was proceeding near Maramma Temple, Doddasomanahalli Village, Thippasandra Hobli, at that time, the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-41-EC-8956, by riding it in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the petitioner, caused the accident and as a result,
petitioner sustained injuries.
Immediately, petitioner was shifted to Government hospital, Magadi, thereafter shifted to Boss hospital wherein he was treated for the injuries sustained by him.

It is stated that, guardian of the minor petitioner has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- for treatment, medicine etc.,
3.
It is further stated that due to the accidental injuries, petitioner has lost his future education and has become dependent.
It is stated that, the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EC-8956.
Hence, the 1 st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
4. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appear before the court and hence, he was placed exparte.
On service of notice, respondents No.2 appeared through its learned counsel and filed the objection statement.
5. The 2nd respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.
It has denied the age of the petitioner and also the amount spent towards medical expenses by the guardian of the minor petitioner.
Also denied the alleged negligence of the rider of the motor cycle and contended that the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the minor petitioner himself.
It is contended that there is delay in lodging the complaint and a false case is foisted by twisting the facts against the insured vehicle.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EC-8956 and contended that the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

It is also contended that the rider of the offending motor cycle was not holding valid and effective driving license on the date of accident and hence, it is not liable to pay the compensation amount.
It is further contended that, the compensation and interest claimed by the guardian of the minor petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, on all these grounds sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, following issues are framed:-
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident alleged to have occurred on 03.12.2018 at about 4.30 p.m., near Maramma Temple, Doddasomanahalli Village, Thippasandra Hobli, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-41-EC-8956 ?

at that time, the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-41-EC-8956, by riding it in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the petitioner, caused the accident and as a result, petitioner sustained injuries.

In order to prove the case mother of the minor petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and reiterated the averments of the petition and got marked F.I.R, F.I.S, Spot Mahazar, IMV report, Wound certificate and Charge Sheet as per Ex.P1 to 6.

and the accident was occurred at 4.30 to p.m. On 03.12.2018 and there is delay of 5 days in lodging the complaint.
The priority is to take treatment and not the lodging of first information.

When the minor petitioner was admitted to the Boss hospital for treatment, then it is the duty of the hospital authority to give information to the police regarding the injuries sustained by him in road traffic accident.

sentences.text: The respondent has disputed the involvement of insured vehicle in the accident.

According to the respondent the accident caused by one red color Hero Honda Splendor vehicle, after lapse of 5 days of the accident in collusion the complaint is filed against TVS Jupiter scooter bearing No.
KA-41-EC-8956.
In support of this contention respondent No.2 examined one witness namely Shobha H. who has investigation the matter and also marked Ex.R3 to R8.

In cross-examination this witness stated that as per statement of the petitioner's mother the accident caused by one red color Hero Honda Spelendour, but the said person is not an eye witnesses to the accident and the said investigator has not examined the eye witness.

On perusal of overall evidence of the Rw2 it is clear that she has not taken any license from GIC and IRDA for investigation and she has not taken the consent of Petitioner and his mother before videography, without giving any information taken photos and videos of the persons is a not a lawful act.
If the insured vehicle was not involved why they kept quite without taking any legal action against the said persons is not answered.
The evidence of the Rw2 is not believable.
14. As far as the defence taken by the respondent is concerned, it remains only as defence without having any backbone.

If at all the petitioner by colluding filed false complaint, then why he has not lodged complaint or taken other legal action against the petitioner and if the police refused to receive the complaint then what prevented him to send through post and to file private complaint before the Magistrate having jurisdiction is not explained.

The respondent has not taken pain to take any action and to produce the same before the tribunal to prove its defence and also not established before the court that the IO in order to help the petitioner filed the false charge sheet against them.
The charge sheet filed by the IO is a corroborative evidence which strengthens the say of the petitioner.
15. On the basis of the said information, the police attached to the High Grounds registered FIR on the same day for the offences punishable U/Sec.279 and 337 of IPC.
According to the petitioner, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the rider of the motorbike bearing Reg No. KA-41-EC-8956.
The IMV report demonstrates that the motorcycle left side indicator dented.
Since the motorcycle hit to the petitioner and he sustained injuries.
As per Mahazar produced at Ex.P3, the total width of the road at the place of accident is 12 ft. and incident occurred at the left side edge of the road and there is curve.

It is true that pedestrians who are intending to cross the road are expected to look either side of the road and venture into crossing the road only after ascertaining that no vehicles are moving on the road.
Since the total width of the road was 12 feet and it is village road, there was sufficient opportunity to the rider to avoid the accident.

The doctrine of reasonable care imposes an obligation on the rider of the motor cycle to take care of the pedestrian on the road and that duty attains a higher degree when the pedestrian happened to be the children of tender years.
In the present case, petitioner is aged 10 years.

Therefore, in the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court rendered in the case of Ravi Kapur vs. State of Rajasthan ((2012) 9 SCC 284), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed as here below:
"The doctrine of reasonable care imposes an obligation or a duty upon a person(for example a driver) to care for the pedestrian on the road and this duty attains a higher Santhosh D.R vs Somashekar H on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4189500/
5 degree

sentences.text: when the pedestrian happen to be children of tender years

. It is axiomatic to say that while driving a vehicle on a public way, there is an implicit duty cast on the drivers to see that their driving does not endanger the life of the right users of the road, may be either vehicular users or pedestrian.
They are expected to take sufficient care to avoid danger to others."

16. In the present case, neither the 1st respondent nor the rider of the motor cycle has contended that, he has tried to avoid the accident either by applying the break or tried to deviate the path of the vehicle.
It is not even contended that child suddenly entered the road.
Therefore, the evidence on record is clear that the rider of the motor cycle failed to take reasonable care to protect the child.

The rider of the motor cycle was expected to recognize the child on the road and he should have taken care at least by predicting that a child will have no sense of danger and he should have slowed down his vehicle.
This omission of the rider of the motor cycle constitutes negligence on his part.
After the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the rider of the motor cycle concluding that the accident was occurred only due to his negligence.
17. The learned counsel for respondent made an effort during the course of cross examination to prove his defence, but failed to obtain favourable answer from the mouth of PW.1.

The evidence of the Rw2 who is investigator is of no use to prove the defence in the absence of documents and also perusal of the evidence of the Rw1 who is the doctor of Magadi Government Hospital and also MLC register it is clearly mentioned that petitioner was sustained injuries in RTA, motorcycle hit against the petitioner.

The documents placed before the tribunal coupled with oral evidence establishes that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-EC-8956 and petitioner sustained injuries in the said accident.
Hence I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:
While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-41-EC-8956.
Therefore, minor petitioner is entitled for the compensation.

Further the learned counsel for the petitioner has asserted that the parents has spent substantial amount towards the treatment and incidental charges like nourishment of the minor and spent huge amount towards the treatment.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner has sustained permanent disability, lost his education and future earnings.

19. While determining the compensation this court has to look into the pain and sufferings, medical expenses, diet, food, nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges and loss of amenities and enjoyment of life that the minor petitioner has suffered, which are discussed herein below.
20. TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY:

The natural guardian of the minor petitioner has alleged that due to injuries sustained in the accident, the minor has become permanently disabled and he is not in a position to do the activities which he used to do prior to the accident.

In order to substantiate the same, guardian of the minor petitioner has produced wound certificate, discharge record, prescriptions, medical bills, advance payment receipts, adhaar cards at Ex.P5, P7 to P29.

sentences.text: The PW.1 has also examined PW.2 who is the Medical Record Technician of Boss hospital and he has produced authorization letter, MLC extract, Case sheet and x-rays which are marked at Ex.P30 to P33.
Further, in order to establish that minor petitioner has suffered physical disability, the petitioner has got examined Dr.S.A. Somashekara as PW.3 and he has produced OPD and X-ray at Ex.P34 and 35.

The petitioner has also examined PW.4 who has produced Ex.P29 and 30 and deposed that, minor petitioner took treatment at Janapriya hospital from 05.12.2021 to 12.12.2021 and has suffered open fracture of the right tibia with tendon injury with open fracture of the right femur and underwent tens nailing for the right tibia.
In the evidence PW.3 has deposed that, the petitioner was diagnosed with Type II Compound fracture of left tibia and he underwent CRIF with TENS nailing on 04.12.2018.
On examination it is found that petitioner walks with pain and limping, wasting of left thigh and diffuse swelling of left leg and surgical and secondary scars are seen over left knee and leg.
The PW.3 in his affidavit has given the physical disability of 29% to the left lower limb and 14% disability to the whole body.

In the affidavit filed by the next friend of the petitioner it is stated that the petitioner is still suffering from mental agony, and has become too weak, he cannot do his regular activities and do normal work as he was doing earlier.
It is pertinent to note that while assessing the disability specially in the case of child victim it is very important to note that for a child the best part of his life is yet to come.

21. Hence, the compensation awarded should enable the child to acquire something or to develop life style which will offset to some extent, the inconvenience or discomfort arising out of the disability.

This means that the tribunal should consider and decide with reference to the evidence:
(i) whether the disablement is permanent or temporary;
(ii) if the disablement is permanent, whether it is permanent total disablement or permanent partial disablement,
(iii) if the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb,
then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body,
that is the permanent disability suffered by the person.
If the Tribunal concludes that there is no permanent disability then there is no question of proceeding further and determining the loss of future earning capacity.

But if the Tribunal Santhosh D.R vs Somashekar H on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4189500/
7 concludes that there is permanent disability

sentences.text: then it will proceed to ascertain its extent.

After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.
Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent ability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood, or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood.
For example, if the left hand of a claimant is amputated, the permanent physical or functional disablement may be assessed around 60%.
If the claimant was a driver or a carpenter, the actual loss of earning capacity may virtually be hundred percent, if he is neither able to drive or do carpentry.

On the other hand, if the claimant was a clerk in government service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be continued as a clerk as he could perform his clerical functions; and in that event the loss of earning capacity will not be 100% as in the case of a driver or carpenter, nor 60% which is the actual physical disability, but far less.

In fact, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of `loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in government service, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities as a consequence of losing his hand.

Sometimes the injured claimant may be continued in service, but may not found suitable for discharging the duties attached to the post or job which he was earlier holding, on account of his disability, and may therefore be shifted to some other suitable but lesser post with lesser emoluments, in which case there should be a limited award under the head of loss of future earning capacity, taking note of the reduced earning capacity.
22. By applying the said precedent to the present case on hand, in this case the petitioner sustained injuries.
The evidence discloses that he is facing some difficulties.
For a student leg is important organ of his body and plays very important role to build up his carrier.
Now as the petitioner has sustained fracture of left tibia, definitely it will have major impact on him in the future.
It is also a set-back for his sports activity.
Hence, this court is of the opinion that the disability has to be taken upto 11% by considering the avocation and age of the petitioner.

23. The reason why the proof of disability and extent of disability is crucial while determining the compensation payable to petitioner is, the petitioner herein is a minor and as per the principle of law laid down in Mallikarjun v. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited and another reported in (2014) 14 SCC 396 while assessing the compensation for pain and sufferings,

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Supreme Court at para No.12 of the said Judgment has held as under:
"Though it is difficult to have an accurate assessment of the compensation in the case of children suffering disability on account of a motor vehicle accident, having regard to the relevant factors, precedents and the approach of various High Courts, we are of the view that the appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, etc. should be, if the disability is above 10% and up to 30% to the whole body, Rs.3 lakhs; up to 60%, Rs.4 lakhs; up to 90%,
Rs.5 lakhs and above 90%, it should be Rs.6 lakhs.

For permanent disability up to 10%, it should be Rs.1 lakh, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take a different yardstick."
24.

As already observed, the petitioner has examined PW.3 who has assessed disability of the petitioner as 14%, but this court considers the disability could be 11% which when compared to the avocation i.e., the petitioner being the student need to carryout his day-to-day activities and other sports.
Hence, the disability is considered at 11%.
In the result he is entitled for the compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- under this head.
25. TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As per the bills marked at Ex.P20 to 24, advance payment receipts at Ex.P25 to 27 and prescriptions at Ex.P12, the PW.1 has spent Rs.30,491/- towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of her cross-examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,491/- under the head of medical expenses.
26. TOWARDS DISCOMFORT, INCONVENIENCE AND LOSS OF EARNINGS TO THE PARENTS DURING THE PERIOD OF HOSPITALISATION :
Looking into the nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner, a maximum of 4 months would have been required for recovery.
Hence the petitioner's parents could not have attended their work for those long period of 4 months.
Therefore this Tribunal deems it expedient to take note of loss of income of parents during the course of treatment and rest of the petitioner.

The same is quantified at Rs.10,000/- p.m. and a sum of Rs.40,000/- (10,000 X 4) is awarded as compensation for discomfort, inconvenience and loss of income to the parents during the period of hospitalization of the minor petitioner.

27. ATTENDANT CHARGES, FOOD, NOURISHMENT & TRAVELLING EXPENSES: The period of hospitalization of 5 days is proved with a help of Ex.P7 discharge summary of Boss hospital from 03.12.2018 to 07.12.2018.
Thus having regard to the age of the petitioner and also the nature of injuries sustained by him, he unavoidably required the service of an attendant for nursing and care.
He must also have been given diet food as suggested by the doctor.
For that the petitioner's family members might have spent some amount towards attendant charges, food, nourishment & travelling expenses.
Accordingly considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,000/- per day.
is awarded under this head.

The 2nd respondent has denied the same.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% p.a.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
31. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that, accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-41-EC-8956.
2nd respondent has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the offending motor cycle.
It is not in dispute that 1 st respondent is the owner and 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending motor cycle.
The respondent No.2 has not proved the breach of any of the policy conditions.
Hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation and 2nd respondent being the insurer shall indemnify respondent No.1 in payment of compensation.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
32. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

This means that the tribunal should consider and decide with reference to the evidence:
(i) whether the disablement is permanent or temporary;
(ii) if the disablement is permanent, whether it is permanent total disablement or permanent partial disablement,
(iii) if the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb,
then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body,
that is the permanent disability suffered by the person.
After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.
The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent ability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood, or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood.
